name: Hypocalcified Amelogenesis Imperfecta

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Amelogenesis Imperfecta

criteria.description: Presence of soft, poorly mineralized enamel that is easily worn or lost
Radiographic evidence of markedly reduced enamel radiodensity compared to dentin
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance
Yellow-brown discoloration of teeth with rapid enamel loss and exposed dentin

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of soft, poorly mineralized enamel with characteristic radiographic findings and clinical enamel loss
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may confirm mutations in enamel matrix genes but is not mandatory for diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Soft, poorly mineralized enamel prone to rapid attrition
Yellow-brown discoloration of enamel due to enamel hypomineralization
Markedly reduced enamel radiodensity on dental radiographs
searchTerms: teeth appear less dense on x-rays
thin enamel visible on dental imaging

laboratory: Normal serum calcium and phosphate levels
imaging: Dental radiographs showing thin or absent enamel layer with normal dentin and pulp chamber
No evidence of systemic bone abnormalities
other: Clinical observation of enamel softness and rapid wear
Family pedigree analysis supporting inheritance pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Enamel is of normal thickness but has mottled opaque appearance
Enamel hardness closer to normal compared to hypocalcified type
Opalescent teeth with bulbous crowns and obliterated pulp chambers

redFlags: Severe enamel loss exposing dentin leading to persistent tooth sensitivity
Rapid progression of enamel breakdown in early childhood
Family history of similar dental enamel defects
